title: Compact auth + streaming snippet playbook for SDK quickstart
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Create a compact, re-usable asset pack and playbook for SDK/API quickstart docs that covers: 1) auth & key best-practices (creation, rotation, scopes), 2) streaming responses (client examples + screenshots for streaming states), and 3) tool-calling visuals (sequence diagrams + blank templates). Assets should be modular (cards, inline code strips, 16:9 hero screenshots) so engineers can copy/paste into docs, README, and blog posts. The aim is to reduce engineering integration friction by providing copy-ready visuals and a short companion doc with micro-guidance and edge-case notes.
acceptance_criteria: A set of 8 PNG/JPG assets (various sizes) that illustrate: API key flow, key rotation, short-lived tokens, streaming lifecycle, and tool-call handshake
Figma file with componentized cards and tokens for rapid edits (public link in ticket)
A single 1-page markdown playbook (docs-snippets.md) with copy-ready code snippets for JS/Go/Python showing auth, streaming client, and a tool call example
Engineering review completed with at most two rounds of feedback and an assigned owner for embedding assets in quickstart pages
Accessibility check completed for color contrast and code ribbon legibility
comments: 2025-02-10 Ava Martinez: Kickoff — scoped to a small, copy-paste friendly asset pack targeted at our SDK quickstart and README. Initial sketch wireframes attached in Figma. Goal: reduce doc author friction and duplicated screenshots across repos.

2025-02-11 Liam O'Connell: Early review — narrowed scope to 3 core flows (auth, streaming, toolcall). Suggests including both long-lived API key and short-lived token flow for private deployments. Flagged potential legal wording for key rotation guidance.

2025-02-12 Priya Kapoor (PM): Notes — prioritize JS and Python snippets in playbook. Add callout about Dedicated/private deployments needing KMS references. Set acceptance criteria for accessibility contrast.

2025-02-13 Design review round 1 — Updated cards: flattened layout for hero and mobile-friendly strip. Feedback from eng: streaming state frames should include connection status examples (connecting, receiving, complete, error).

2025-02-14 Engineering review (Brandon Chen): Implementation note — avoid showing actual key values; provide placeholders and CLI commands for key rotation (rbac links). Eng requested a minimal non-blocking change to streaming snippet to show reconnect/backoff example. Logged GH PR for snippet updates: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/472

2025-02-15 Ava Martinez: Design round 2 — Finalized asset exports (PNG/WebP) and uploaded docs-snippets.md to the drive. Prepared handoff checklist for docs engineers and content owners. Next: accessibility pass and final sign-off from PM.
follow_up_tasks: Assign docs engineer to embed assets in /docs/quickstart/sdk.md
Add automated screenshot check to docs CI to prevent regressions
Schedule a 30m handoff session with solutions engineering to explain token rotation visuals
notes: Trade-offs considered: full animated GIF vs static frames. Chose static strips + simulated micro-animations in CSS for faster page load and easier reuse across PDFs. We intentionally kept color palette aligned with docs brand colors to avoid extra CSS overrides. Kept file sizes under 200KB for hero PNG exports.
